column1: 1:1|The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.|Retain authorial royal attribution.
1:2|For learning wisdom and discipline,\nfor understanding words of insight;|Preserve paired aims of collection.
1:3|for receiving discipline that teaches good judgment,\nrighteousness, justice, and fairness;|Keep three ethical terms distinct.
1:4|for giving the inexperienced good sense,\nand a young man knowledge and discretion.|Retain specifically masculine learner and practical shrewdness.
1:5|Let the wise listen and add to their learning;\nlet the discerning gain guidance,|Experienced readers also learn.
1:6|to understand proverbs and figures of speech,\nthe words of the wise and their riddles.|Retain varied literary forms.
1:7|The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge;\nfools despise wisdom and discipline.|Keep fear and beginning as foundational vocabulary.
1:8|My son, listen to your father’s discipline,\nand do not abandon your mother’s instruction.|Both parents teach with distinct terms.
1:9|They are a lovely garland for your head\nand ornaments for your neck.|Preserve adornment imagery.
1:10|My son, if sinners entice you,\ndo not agree to go.|Consent is the immediate warning.
1:11|They may say, “Come with us!\nLet’s lie in wait to spill blood;\nlet’s ambush someone innocent for no reason.|Do not soften proposed gratuitous violence.
1:12|Let’s swallow them alive, like Sheol,\nwhole, like those going down to the Pit.|Keep death images and whole-person swallowing.
1:13|We will find all kinds of precious wealth\nand fill our houses with plunder.|Preserve the lure of stolen wealth.
1:14|Throw in your lot with us;\nwe will all share one purse.”|Retain lot and common purse images.
1:15|My son, do not walk their road;\nkeep your feet off their path.|Road imagery begins sustained contrast.
1:16|Their feet run toward evil;\nthey hurry to spill blood.|Keep speed and explicit bloodshed.
1:17|A net is spread in vain\nin full view of any bird.|Preserve the proverb’s bird comparison.
1:18|But these men lie in wait for their own blood;\nthey ambush their own lives.|Make self-destructive reversal explicit.
1:19|Such are the paths of everyone greedy for gain:\nit takes the life of those who possess it.|Gain itself becomes fatal agent.
1:20|Wisdom cries out in the street;\nshe raises her voice in the public squares.|Introduce Wisdom as female speaker.
1:21|At the head of the noisy streets she calls;\nat the city gates she speaks her words:|Public proclamation remains concrete.
1:22|“How long, you inexperienced ones, will you love inexperience?\nHow long will scoffers delight in scoffing\nand fools hate knowledge?|Retain three audiences and deliberate repetition.
1:23|Turn when I rebuke you!\nThen I will pour out my spirit to you\nand make my words known to you.|Preserve spirit image rather than reducing to information.
1:24|I called, but you refused;\nI stretched out my hand, but no one paid attention.|Keep both unanswered gestures.
1:25|You dismissed all my counsel\nand would have none of my rebuke.|Retain counsel and rebuke distinction.
1:26|So I too will laugh at your disaster;\nI will mock when terror comes upon you,|Wisdom’s disturbing response remains explicit.
1:27|when terror sweeps over you like devastation\nand disaster arrives like a whirlwind,\nwhen distress and anguish come upon you.|Follow read form and retain accumulating disaster clauses.
1:28|Then they will call me, but I will not answer;\nthey will search for me, but will not find me.|Retain shift from you to they.
1:29|Because they hated knowledge\nand did not choose the fear of the LORD,|Preserve stated grounds and choice.
1:30|because they wanted none of my counsel\nand rejected every rebuke I gave,|Keep repeated rejected counsel.
1:31|they will eat the fruit of their own way\nand have their fill of their own schemes.|Preserve eating metaphor and self-chosen consequences.
1:32|The turning away of the inexperienced kills them;\nthe complacency of fools destroys them.|Different failures remain distinct.
1:33|But whoever listens to me will live securely,\nat ease, without fear of disaster.”|Close Wisdom’s speech with security promise.
2:1|My son, if you receive my words\nand store up my commands within you,|Begin extended conditional sentence.
2:2|making your ear attentive to wisdom\nand turning your heart toward understanding,|Preserve ear and heart images.
2:3|if you call out for insight\nand raise your voice for understanding,|Retain repeated active appeal.
2:4|if you seek it like silver\nand search for it like buried treasure,|Keep economic search comparison.
2:5|then you will understand the fear of the LORD\nand find the knowledge of God.|Mark delayed then answering verses 1–4.
2:6|For the LORD gives wisdom;\nknowledge and understanding come from his mouth.|Wisdom’s source remains divine speech.
2:7|He stores up sound wisdom for the upright;\nhe is a shield for those who walk with integrity,|Follow read form; retain shield and integrity.
2:8|guarding the paths of justice\nand protecting the way of his faithful ones.|Follow plural read form for faithful ones.
2:9|Then you will understand righteousness, justice, and fairness—\nevery good path.|Repeat ethical triad from 1:3.
2:10|For wisdom will enter your heart,\nand knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.|Retain inner reception and pleasure.
2:11|Discretion will watch over you;\nunderstanding will guard you,|Wisdom terms act as guardians.
2:12|rescuing you from the way of evil,\nfrom the man whose speech is twisted,|Retain male agent and speech distortion.
2:13|from those who leave straight paths\nto walk along dark ways,|Keep straight/dark contrast.
2:14|who rejoice in doing evil\nand delight in evil’s perversity,|Preserve enjoyment of wrongdoing.
2:15|whose paths are crooked\nand whose courses are devious.|Keep paired path metaphors.
2:16|Wisdom will also rescue you from the forbidden woman,\nfrom the outsider whose words are smooth,|Contextual sexual outsider; do not assert foreign ethnicity.
2:17|who abandons the companion of her youth\nand forgets the covenant of her God.|Keep companion and divine covenant without narrowing covenant’s referent.
2:18|Her house sinks toward death,\nand her paths lead to the shades of the dead.|Preserve descent and dead shades.
2:19|None who go to her return\nor reach the paths of life.|Keep warning’s absolute poetic force.
2:20|So you will walk in the way of the good\nand keep to the paths of the righteous.|Connect rescue to positive way.
2:21|For the upright will dwell in the land,\nand those of integrity will remain in it;|Keep land rather than spiritualizing place.
2:22|but the wicked will be cut off from the land,\nand the faithless will be uprooted from it.|Retain exclusion and uprooting images.
3:1|My son, do not forget my instruction;\nlet your heart keep my commands.|Retain parental instruction rather than silently making divine speech.
3:2|They will add length of days, years of life,\nand peace to you.|Keep duration and peace together.
3:3|Let faithful love and faithfulness never leave you.\nBind them around your neck;\nwrite them on the tablet of your heart.|Preserve paired virtues and inscription image.
3:4|Then you will find favor and a good reputation\nin the eyes of God and people.|Render good understanding contextually as reputation.
3:5|Trust in the LORD with all your heart;\ndo not lean on your own understanding.|Keep trust and leaning image.
3:6|Know him in all your ways,\nand he will make your paths straight.|Retain relational know rather than mere acknowledgment.
3:7|Do not be wise in your own eyes;\nfear the LORD and turn away from evil.|Keep self-estimation and ethical turning.
3:8|This will bring healing to your body\nand refreshment to your bones.|Body renders navel idiom; document concrete Hebrew in note.
3:9|Honor the LORD with your wealth\nand with the first of all your produce.|Retain first produce rather than generic generosity.
3:10|Then your barns will be filled with plenty,\nand your vats will overflow with new wine.|Preserve agricultural abundance.
3:11|My son, do not reject the LORD’s discipline\nor resent his correction.|Keep correction as painful but not unspecified punishment.
3:12|For the LORD corrects the one he loves,\nlike a father the son he delights in.|Retain father-son comparison and delight.
3:13|Happy is the person who finds wisdom,\nthe person who gains understanding.|Keep wisdom’s human beneficiary broad.
3:14|Her profit is better than silver’s;\nher yield is better than gold.|Feminine Wisdom and trade imagery remain.
3:15|She is more precious than jewels;\nnothing you desire can compare with her.|Follow read form peninim; exact precious material uncertain.
3:16|Long life is in her right hand;\nin her left are wealth and honor.|Retain right/left allocation.
3:17|Her ways are pleasant ways,\nand all her paths are peace.|Preserve repeated ways and comprehensive peace.
3:18|She is a tree of life to those who grasp her;\nthose who hold her fast are happy.|Keep tree of life as biblical image.
3:19|By wisdom the LORD founded the earth;\nby understanding he established the heavens.|Retain creation through wisdom parallel.
3:20|By his knowledge the deeps broke open,\nand the clouds drip dew.|Preserve deeps and dew rather than general rain.
3:21|My son, do not let these slip from your sight:\nguard sound wisdom and discretion.|Keep referential these with following specification.
3:22|They will be life for your soul\nand an adornment for your neck.|Retain life and necklace imagery.
3:23|Then you will walk your road securely,\nand your foot will not stumble.|Security remains in path image.
3:24|When you lie down, you will not be afraid;\nyou will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.|Preserve repetition and restful image.
3:25|Do not fear sudden terror\nor the devastation of the wicked when it comes.|Leave devastation’s relation to wicked open.
3:26|For the LORD will be at your side\nand keep your foot from being caught.|Choose side for ambiguous confidence/side term; retain trap.
3:27|Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due\nwhen it is in your power to act.|Follow singular hand read form through power idiom.
3:28|Do not tell your neighbor, “Go away and come back;\nI will give it tomorrow,” when you have it now.|Follow singular neighbor and expose needless delay.
3:29|Do not plot harm against your neighbor\nwho lives beside you in trust.|Preserve betrayed trust.
3:30|Do not quarrel with someone for no reason\nwhen that person has done you no harm.|Keep cause qualification rather than universal ban on dispute.
3:31|Do not envy a violent man\nor choose any of his ways.|Retain violence as specific evil.
3:32|For the devious are detestable to the LORD,\nbut the upright share his confidence.|Keep moral contrast and intimacy of counsel.
3:33|The LORD’s curse is on the house of the wicked,\nbut he blesses the home of the righteous.|Retain explicit curse and household contrast.
3:34|He scoffs at scoffers,\nbut gives grace to the humble.|Follow humble read form; keep reciprocal scoffing.
3:35|The wise inherit honor,\nbut fools carry away disgrace.|Resolve difficult lifting verb contextually without erasing shame.
4:1|Sons, listen to a father’s discipline;\npay attention and learn understanding.|Retain plural sons and parental voice.
4:2|For I give you good teaching;\ndo not abandon my instruction.|Preserve teacher’s claim to good instruction.
4:3|When I was a son with my father,\ntender and the only one in my mother’s sight,|Keep remembered unique relationship, not infer family genealogy.
4:4|he taught me and said,\n“Let your heart hold fast to my words;\nkeep my commands and live.|Mark quoted father within father’s address.
4:5|Get wisdom; get understanding.\nDo not forget or turn away from what I say.|Preserve repeated acquisition imperative.
4:6|Do not abandon her, and she will guard you;\nlove her, and she will protect you.|Feminine personification stays visible.
4:7|The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom!\nWhatever else you acquire, get understanding.|Retain paradoxical beginning and acquisition repetition.
4:8|Cherish her, and she will raise you up;\nembrace her, and she will honor you.|Preserve reciprocal elevation and embrace.
4:9|She will place a lovely garland on your head\nand present you with a beautiful crown.”|Close recalled paternal speech with adornment.
4:10|Listen, my son, and receive my words;\nthen your years of life will multiply.|Return direct instruction and longevity.
4:11|I have taught you the way of wisdom;\nI have led you on straight paths.|Retain teacher’s paired actions.
4:12|As you walk, your steps will not be cramped;\nwhen you run, you will not stumble.|Preserve walking/running progression.
4:13|Hold tightly to discipline; do not let go.\nGuard her, for she is your life.|Preserve feminine discipline and urgent grip.
4:14|Do not enter the path of the wicked;\ndo not proceed along the way of evildoers.|Retain parallel avoidance warnings.
4:15|Avoid it; do not pass along it.\nTurn away from it and move on.|Keep four short imperatives.
4:16|For they cannot sleep unless they do evil;\nthey lose sleep unless they make someone fall.|Follow causative read form; keep addiction to harm.
4:17|They eat the bread of wickedness\nand drink the wine of violence.|Retain literal food imagery for wrongdoing.
4:18|But the path of the righteous is like dawn’s light,\nshining ever brighter until full day.|Preserve growing light comparison.
4:19|The way of the wicked is deep darkness;\nthey do not know what makes them stumble.|Keep unrecognized cause of fall.
4:20|My son, pay attention to my words;\nturn your ear to what I say.|Retain attention and hearing parallel.
4:21|Do not let them leave your sight;\nkeep them within your heart.|Preserve eye/heart sequence.
4:22|For they are life to those who find them\nand healing to their whole body.|Keep bodily healing scope.
4:23|Above all that you guard, guard your heart,\nfor from it flow the springs of life.|Retain guarding repetition and life-source image.
4:24|Put twisted speech away from you;\nkeep devious talk far from your lips.|Preserve crooked speech warning.
4:25|Let your eyes look straight ahead,\nyour gaze directly before you.|Keep paired visual focus.
4:26|Make level the path for your feet,\nand let all your ways be firm.|Select leveling sense while retaining established paths.
4:27|Do not turn to the right or the left;\nturn your foot away from evil.|Keep directional contrast and final ethical turn.
5:1|My son, pay attention to my wisdom;\nturn your ear to my understanding,|Retain personal teaching voice.
5:2|so that you may guard discretion\nand your lips may preserve knowledge.|Knowledge shapes speech as well as thought.
5:3|The forbidden woman’s lips drip honey,\nand her mouth is smoother than oil,|Keep sensual comparisons.
5:4|but in the end she is bitter as wormwood,\nsharp as a two-edged sword.|Retain plant bitterness and weapon.
5:5|Her feet go down to death;\nher steps lead straight to Sheol.|Keep death and Sheol parallel.
5:6|She does not weigh the path of life;\nher courses wander, and she does not know it.|Choose feminine subject amid ambiguous second/third person form.
5:7|Now, sons, listen to me;\ndo not turn away from what I say.|Preserve plural address.
5:8|Keep your way far from her;\ndo not approach the door of her house,|Distance is physical in the image.
5:9|or you will give your honor to others\nand your years to someone cruel;|Do not specify an unnamed cruel person.
5:10|strangers will feast on your strength,\nand your hard-earned goods will end up in another’s house.|Preserve exploitation of effort.
5:11|At your end you will groan,\nwhen your flesh and body waste away.|Keep bodily consequences without diagnosing disease.
5:12|You will say, “How I hated discipline!\nHow my heart despised correction!|Retain lamenting self-recognition.
5:13|I did not listen to my teachers\nor turn my ear to those who instructed me.|Keep paired failures to listen.
5:14|I was nearly in utter ruin\nin the midst of the gathered community.”|Preserve nearly and public setting.
5:15|Drink water from your own cistern,\nflowing water from your own well.|Retain sexual imagery rather than replacing it with explanation.
5:16|Should your springs spill out into the streets,\nyour streams of water into the public squares?|Read contextual rhetorical question; note alternative assertion.
5:17|Let them be yours alone,\nnot shared with strangers.|Keep exclusivity within sustained image.
5:18|May your fountain be blessed;\nrejoice in the wife of your youth,|Identify marriage without flattening fountain.
5:19|a loving doe, a graceful mountain goat.\nMay her breasts satisfy you at all times;\nmay her love always intoxicate you.|Preserve explicit breasts and animal imagery.
5:20|Why, my son, be intoxicated with a forbidden woman\nand embrace the breast of an outsider?|Retain repeated intoxication and breast.
5:21|For a man’s ways are before the LORD’s eyes;\nhe weighs all his paths.|Keep divine scrutiny and weighing.
5:22|The wicked man’s own wrongs capture him;\nthe cords of his sin hold him fast.|Preserve self-entanglement.
5:23|He dies for lack of discipline;\nhis great folly leads him astray.|Retain folly rather than intoxication as sole sense here.
6:1|My son, if you have guaranteed your neighbor’s debt,\nif you have clasped hands in a pledge to a stranger,|Explain financial surety while retaining hand pledge.
6:2|you are snared by the words of your mouth,\ncaught by the words of your mouth.|Keep emphatic repetition.

6:3|Then do this, my son, and free yourself,\nfor you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands:\ngo, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.|Preserve urgent humiliating appeal, not evasion of obligation.
6:4|Give your eyes no sleep\nand your eyelids no rest.|Keep bodily parallel.
6:5|Free yourself like a gazelle from the hunter’s hand,\nlike a bird from the trapper’s hand.|Hunter supplied for implicit first hand; retain animal parallels.
6:6|Go to the ant, you sluggard;\nstudy her ways and become wise.|Keep sharp address and observation.
6:7|She has no commander,\nno overseer or ruler,|Preserve three absent authorities.
6:8|yet she prepares her food in summer\nand gathers her provisions at harvest.|Keep seasonal foresight.
6:9|How long will you lie there, you sluggard?\nWhen will you rise from sleep?|Retain questions rather than advice paraphrase.
6:10|“A little sleep, a little rest,\na little folding of the hands to lie down”—|Preserve threefold little.
6:11|and poverty will come upon you like a prowler,\nneed like a man with a shield.|Retain armed shield image; prowler expresses approaching figure.
6:12|A worthless person, a man of wrongdoing,\ngoes about with twisted speech,|Keep male description and corrupt speech.
6:13|winking his eyes, signaling with his feet,\npointing with his fingers.|Preserve all three bodily signals.
6:14|With perversity in his heart he plots evil continually;\nhe stirs up conflict.|Follow read form for conflict.
6:15|Therefore disaster will come upon him suddenly;\nin an instant he will be broken beyond healing.|Keep suddenness and irreversible break.
6:16|There are six things the LORD hates,\nseven that are detestable to him:|Preserve ascending numerical formula.
6:17|haughty eyes, a lying tongue,\nhands that spill innocent blood,|Keep body-part list and real killing.
6:18|a heart that devises wicked plans,\nfeet that hurry to run toward evil,|Continue parallel anatomical catalogue.
6:19|a false witness who breathes out lies,\nand someone who stirs up conflict among brothers.|Retain brothers and repeated conflict.
6:20|My son, keep your father’s command\nand do not abandon your mother’s instruction.|Preserve both parental authorities.
6:21|Bind them always to your heart;\nfasten them around your neck.|Keep binding images.
6:22|When you walk, instruction will lead you;\nwhen you lie down, it will guard you;\nwhen you wake, it will speak with you.|Supply instruction for feminine subject; preserve three occasions.
6:23|For the command is a lamp, and instruction is light;\ncorrective discipline is the way of life,|Retain light and path metaphors.
6:24|keeping you from the evil woman,\nfrom the smooth tongue of the outsider.|Do not merge evil woman and ethnic foreigner.
6:25|Do not desire her beauty in your heart\nor let her capture you with her eyes.|Eyes renders eyelids metonym while preserving seduction.
6:26|For a prostitute’s price is a loaf of bread,\nbut another man’s wife hunts a precious life.|Select price reading; note alternative reduction to a loaf.
6:27|Can a man scoop fire into his lap\nwithout burning his clothes?|Preserve concrete rhetorical question.
6:28|Can a man walk on hot coals\nwithout scorching his feet?|Keep second fire comparison.
6:29|So it is with one who goes to his neighbor’s wife;\nno one who touches her will go unpunished.|Retain specific adultery and consequences.
6:30|People do not despise a thief who steals\nto satisfy his hunger,|Keep sympathetic motive without excusing theft.
6:31|but if caught, he must repay sevenfold,\neven giving all the wealth of his house.|Preserve sevenfold rather than harmonizing other laws.
6:32|A man who commits adultery lacks sense;\nhe who does it destroys his own life.|Retain male responsibility.
6:33|He will find wounds and dishonor;\nhis disgrace will not be wiped away.|Keep physical and social harm.
6:34|For jealousy fuels a husband’s fury,\nand he will show no pity on the day of vengeance.|Preserve dangerous retaliation without endorsing it.
6:35|He will accept no compensation;\nhe will refuse, however large your gift.|Keep refusal of monetary settlement.
7:1|My son, keep my words;\nstore up my commands within you.|Retain instruction as stored treasure.
7:2|Keep my commands and live;\nguard my instruction like the pupil of your eye.|Preserve vulnerable-eye image.
7:3|Bind them to your fingers;\nwrite them on the tablet of your heart.|Keep both physical inscriptions.
7:4|Say to Wisdom, “You are my sister,”\nand call Understanding your close relative,|Preserve female kinship personification.
7:5|so they may guard you from the forbidden woman,\nfrom the outsider whose words are smooth.|Retain relationship between wisdom and protection.
7:6|At the window of my house\nI looked out through the lattice.|Keep first-person observer and architecture.
7:7|Among the inexperienced I saw,\namong the youths I noticed, a young man without sense.|Retain selective observation of one male.
7:8|He crossed the street near her corner\nand headed along the road to her house,|Preserve deliberate movement.
7:9|at twilight, as the day faded,\nin the dark heart of the night.|Retain intensifying darkness.
7:10|Then a woman came to meet him,\ndressed like a prostitute, her intentions concealed.|Do not identify married woman as professional prostitute.
7:11|She is loud and defiant;\nher feet never stay at home.|Keep characterization within narrator’s scene.
7:12|Now in the street, now in the squares,\nshe lies in wait at every corner.|Preserve repeated locations and ambush.
7:13|She seized him and kissed him;\nwith a bold face she said,|Retain physical initiative.
7:14|“I had fellowship offerings to make;\ntoday I fulfilled my vows.|Preserve ritual context without asserting its sincerity.
7:15|That is why I came out to meet you,\nto search eagerly for you—and I found you!|Keep flattering claim of personal pursuit.
7:16|I have spread coverings on my couch,\npatterned linen from Egypt.|Retain imported textile detail.
7:17|I have perfumed my bed\nwith myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.|Preserve three aromatics.
7:18|Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning;\nlet us delight in lovemaking.|Keep explicit sexual invitation and drinking image.
7:19|The man is not at home;\nhe has gone on a long journey.|Preserve distancing the man rather than inserting husband in speech.
7:20|He took a bag of silver with him;\nhe will not return home until the full moon.”|Retain money and calendar marker.
7:21|With much persuasion she turned him;\nwith smooth lips she drew him away.|Preserve agency and paired speech tactics.
7:22|All at once he follows her,\nlike an ox going to slaughter,\nlike a fool in fetters going to correction,|Keep difficult fetters/fool wording rather than conjectured animal.
7:23|until an arrow pierces his liver;\nlike a bird darting into a trap,\nhe does not know that his life is at stake.|Retain liver, bird, and life consequence.
7:24|Now, sons, listen to me;\npay attention to the words of my mouth.|Return to plural audience.
7:25|Do not let your heart turn toward her ways;\ndo not stray onto her paths.|Keep inner inclination and outer path.
7:26|For many are the wounded she has brought down;\nher slain are a mighty host.|Retain many slain; strength/numerous ambiguity noted.
7:27|Her house is a road to Sheol,\ngoing down to the chambers of death.|Keep underworld architecture.
8:1|Does not Wisdom call out?\nDoes not Understanding raise her voice?|Maintain female public countervoice.
8:2|On the heights beside the road,\nat the crossroads, she takes her stand.|Keep accessible public locations.
8:3|Beside the city gates, at the entrance,\nat the open doorways, she cries:|Preserve triple threshold imagery.
8:4|“To you, people, I call;\nmy voice goes out to all humankind.|Keep broad human audience.
8:5|You inexperienced ones, learn good sense;\nyou fools, learn understanding.|Different learners share invitation.
8:6|Listen, for I speak worthy things;\nwhat comes from my lips is right.|Retain quality and rightness of speech.
8:7|My mouth speaks truth;\nwickedness is detestable to my lips.|Keep truth and moral rejection.
8:8|All the words of my mouth are righteous;\nthere is nothing twisted or crooked in them.|Preserve path-like speech adjectives.
8:9|They are all straightforward to the discerning\nand right to those who find knowledge.|Retain reception-dependent clarity.
8:10|Receive my discipline rather than silver,\nknowledge rather than choice gold.|Keep preference rather than blanket rejection of wealth.
8:11|For wisdom is better than jewels;\nno desirable thing can compare with her.|Maintain feminine reference within speech.
8:12|I, Wisdom, dwell with good sense;\nI find knowledge and discretion.|Retain self-identification and associated qualities.
8:13|The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil.\nI hate pride, arrogance, the evil way,\nand twisted speech.|Keep hatred’s explicit objects.
8:14|Counsel and sound wisdom are mine;\nI am understanding; strength is mine.|Retain Wisdom’s first-person claims.
8:15|Through me kings reign\nand rulers decree what is just.|Preserve political and judicial function.
8:16|Through me princes govern,\nand nobles—all who judge rightly.|Follow pinned righteousness reading, not earth alternative.
8:17|I love those who love me,\nand those who seek me will find me.|Follow my lovers read form.
8:18|Wealth and honor are with me,\nenduring riches and righteousness.|Keep righteousness alongside material wealth.
8:19|My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold;\nmy yield surpasses choice silver.|Retain fruit/yield economic imagery.
8:20|I walk on the path of righteousness,\nalong the ways of justice,|Keep moral path vocabulary.
8:21|giving substance as an inheritance to those who love me\nand filling their treasuries.|Preserve possessions rather than abstract reality alone.
8:22|The LORD acquired me at the beginning of his way,\nbefore his works of long ago.|Retain qanah as acquired; note created/possessed possibilities.
8:23|From ages past I was established,\nfrom the beginning, before the earth.|Keep ancient establishment without later doctrinal additions.
8:24|When there were no deeps, I was brought forth,\nwhen there were no springs heavy with water.|Preserve birth imagery and primeval water.
8:25|Before the mountains were set in place,\nbefore the hills, I was brought forth,|Repeat birth verb exactly.
8:26|before he made earth and open country\nor the first dust of the world.|Retain creation sequence and dust.
8:27|When he established the heavens, I was there;\nwhen he traced a circle on the face of the deep,|Keep presence and horizon circle.
8:28|when he made firm the clouds above,\nwhen the springs of the deep grew strong,|Retain source’s strong springs without adding fountains burst.
8:29|when he set the sea its boundary\nso the waters would not cross his command,\nwhen he marked out the earth’s foundations,|Keep boundary, command, foundations.
8:30|I was beside him as a master worker.\nI was his delight day after day,\nplaying before him at all times,|Choose craftsman sense of amon; flag child alternative.
8:31|playing in his inhabited world,\ndelighting in humankind.|Preserve playful rejoicing and human delight.
8:32|Now, sons, listen to me;\nhappy are those who keep my ways.|Return to sons and happiness.
8:33|Listen to discipline and become wise;\ndo not reject it.|Retain invitation and refusal warning.
8:34|Happy is the person who listens to me,\nwatching at my doors day after day,\nwaiting at my doorposts.|Keep threshold vigilance and repetition.
8:35|For whoever finds me finds life\nand obtains favor from the LORD.|Follow finds read form.
8:36|But whoever misses me harms his own life;\nall who hate me love death.”|Keep missing/sinning ambiguity through misses; retain stark death contrast.
9:1|Wisdom has built her house;\nshe has carved out its seven pillars.|Retain seven without symbolic exposition.
9:2|She has slaughtered her animals, mixed her wine,\nand set her table.|Keep three banquet preparations.
9:3|She has sent out her young women;\nshe calls from the city’s highest places,|Retain female messengers and public appeal.
9:4|“Whoever is inexperienced, turn in here!”\nTo one who lacks sense she says,|Match invitation later echoed by Folly.
9:5|“Come, eat my bread\nand drink the wine I have mixed.|Keep meal invitation.
9:6|Leave inexperience behind and live;\nwalk straight along the way of understanding.”|Choose inexperience as object while retaining path.
9:7|Whoever disciplines a scoffer brings dishonor on himself;\nwhoever corrects the wicked receives abuse.|Keep corrective action’s danger.
9:8|Do not correct a scoffer, or he will hate you;\ncorrect a wise person, and he will love you.|Retain contrast requiring discernment.
9:9|Give instruction to the wise, and they become wiser;\nteach the righteous, and they add to their learning.|Keep wise/righteous parallel.
9:10|The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom,\nand knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.|Choose divine referent for plural holy ones; note ambiguity.
